msg: Art. 30(2)(a): no clear and complete description of all functions and ICT services. Add: 'A clear and complete description of all the functions and ICT services to be provided is set out in Schedule 1.'
any: clear and complete description of all the functions and ict services
complete description of the ict services

msg: Art. 30(2)(a) / Art. 29: the contract never states whether subcontracting of a critical or important function is permitted and under which conditions. Add a 'Conditions for subcontracting' clause.
Art. 30(2)(b): the regions and countries where the services are provided and where data is processed and stored are not named, and no notice of change is required.
any: countries where the services will be provided

msg: Art. 30(2)(c): missing the data protection wording. DORA asks literally for 'availability, authenticity, integrity and confidentiality' of data.
Art. 30(2)(d): no guarantee of access, recovery and return of data on insolvency, resolution or discontinuation of the provider, in an easily accessible format.
Art. 30(2)(e): no service level descriptions, including updates and revisions.
Art. 30(2)(f): incident assistance must be 'at no additional cost, or at a cost that is determined ex-ante'. Neither phrase is in this contract.
Art. 30(2)(g): the provider is not obliged to fully cooperate with the competent authorities and resolution authorities of the financial entity.
any: cooperate fully with the competent authorit

msg: Art. 30(2)(h): termination rights without a stated minimum notice period. Name the period in days.
Art. 30(2)(i): no conditions for the provider's participation in ICT security awareness programmes and digital operational resilience training.
Art. 30(3)(a): for a critical or important function the SLA needs precise quantitative and qualitative performance targets, not a generic uptime line.
Art. 30(3)(b): no notice periods and reporting obligations for developments that might have a material impact on the provider's ability to deliver.
Art. 30(3)(c): the provider is not required to implement and test business contingency plans, nor to hold ICT security measures, tools and policies.
any: contingency plans and to have in place

msg: Art. 30(3)(d): no obligation to participate and fully cooperate in the financial entity's threat-led penetration testing (TLPT).
Art. 30(3)(e): no unrestricted rights of access, inspection and audit for the financial entity, its appointed third party and the competent authority.
Art. 30(3)(f): no exit strategy with a mandatory adequate transition period. This is the clause supervisors ask for first.
Art. 30(1): the arrangement must be set out in writing in one single written document available to the parties on paper or in a downloadable, durable and accessible format.
Art. 28(7): the contract lists no grounds for termination (significant breach of law, impediments to monitoring, weaknesses in ICT risk management, supervisory finding).
Art. 30(3)(e) says the audit rights are unrestricted; this line caps them to a fixed number of audits per year. Supervisors read a cap as a missing clause.
Art. 30(2)(f) allows only 'no additional cost' or a cost fixed ex-ante; open-ended incident billing (time and materials, then-current rates) does not qualify.
Art. 30(2)(b): the data location must be named as regions and countries. An open-ended location clause cannot be entered in the register of information.
Art. 30(2)(b) and Art. 29: changes of location or of subcontractors without notice remove the financial entity's ability to monitor. Replace with a stated notice period.
